name: Our Lady of Fatima
history: From 13 May to 13 October 1917, Our Lady appeared six times to three shepherd children at the Cova da Iria near Fátima in Portugal, asking for prayer, penance and the daily Rosary. The apparitions were approved by the local bishop in 1930. Two of the children, Francisco and Jacinta Marto, were canonised in 2017.
life: Lúcia dos Santos, aged ten, and her cousins Francisco and Jacinta Marto, eight and seven, were minding sheep when, they said, a lady brighter than the sun appeared above a holm oak. She asked them to return on the thirteenth of each month, to pray the Rosary every day for peace and the end of the war, and to offer sacrifices for sinners. The children suffered disbelief, threats and even a short imprisonment. In July they were shown a vision of hell and given a message asking for devotion to the Immaculate Heart of Mary. On 13 October a large crowd, tens of thousands strong, reported seeing the sun dance in the sky. Francisco and Jacinta died young in the influenza epidemic; Lúcia became a Carmelite and died in 2005. John Paul II, shot on 13 May 1981, believed Our Lady had saved his life. As with all approved apparitions, belief in them is not required, but they are a trustworthy call to the Gospel.
prayerTo: Our Lady of Fatima, you asked three children to pray and to make sacrifices for sinners, and they answered with generous hearts. Teach me to pray the Rosary faithfully, to offer my small sufferings for others, and to take refuge in your Immaculate Heart. Pray for peace in the world. Amen.
penance: Pray the Rosary today for peace, and make one small sacrifice for sinners, as the children did: a drink of water given up, or a complaint left unsaid.
meditation: The children were asked to offer small sacrifices for others. What small, hidden sacrifice could you make today for someone far from God?
